Metric definitions
FIP
Fielding Independent Pitching. What the ERA would be if every ball in play were league-average: only strikeouts, walks, hit batsmen and home runs appear, because those are the outcomes seven fielders and a bounce cannot touch. Scaled to look like an ERA by adding a league constant.
xFIP
FIP with the pitcher’s actual home runs thrown away and replaced by his fly balls at the league HR/FB rate. HR/FB is the least stable thing a pitcher does over a season, so normalising it is what turns FIP from a description into a forecast.
SIERA
Skill-Interactive ERA. The heaviest-weighted input here. Unlike FIP it accounts for the type of contact and for the interactions between them: strikeouts get more valuable as they pile up, walks get worse in company, and a ground-ball profile is worth more to a pitcher who also misses bats. The published formula’s squared net-ground-ball term flips sign with the sign of the term itself, which rewards extreme ground-ball and extreme fly-ball pitchers over the ones in the middle.
K-BB%
Strikeout rate minus walk rate, per plate appearance. The cleanest single separator of dominant from wild, and by some distance the fastest of these to stabilise — early in a season it is carrying the estimate on its own while the ERA estimators are still noise.
xwOBA
Expected weighted on-base average allowed, from Statcast exit velocity and launch angle. Measures the quality of contact given up rather than whether it found a glove. The run projection is built from this rather than from hits, which is how contact quality reaches the number at all.
Stuff (proxy)
A 100-is-average grade for raw pitch characteristics — velocity, movement and extension against the league mean for that pitch type. It is not FanGraphs’ Stuff+ or Pitching+, which are proprietary models with no free feed; it is a lighter-weight stand-in built from the same public Statcast inputs, and it carries the smallest weight in the skill score accordingly.
SwStr%
Swinging strikes as a share of total pitches. A direct read on missing bats, and it stabilises faster than the strikeout rate it feeds.
ERA+ / FIP−
Both put a pitcher on a 100-is-average scale after taking his home park out of it, and they point in opposite directions by convention: above 100 is good for ERA+, below 100 is good for FIP−. Both are shown rather than picking one.
WHIP
Walks plus hits per inning pitched. A clean baserunner count with no pretensions to being predictive.
ERA
Earned runs per nine. Preventing runs is the job, so it is the honest scoreboard — but over a dozen starts it is heavily a story about defence and sequencing, which is why the board scores on SIERA and xFIP and shows ERA alongside them rather than instead.
Start score
Skill (72%) blended with today’s context (28%), 1–100. Context is the opposing lineup, park, weather and home/road, and 50 is neutral.
Projection
Per-batter rates are combined with the opposing lineup by odds ratio (log5), the outing length is projected from the pitch-count leash, and the two are multiplied. Runs come from xwOBA through linear weights instead, so runs and hits can disagree slightly — deliberately.
P(over) and Edge
Counts are given a negative binomial fitted to the projected mean and variance (a normal for outs), so the tail is honest rather than Poisson-thin. Edge is how far past the −110 break-even of 52.4% the model sits on its preferred side; inside that band the board says PASS.
Why Diff and the pick disagree
On runs, walks and hits the distribution is right-skewed — a start is usually two runs and occasionally seven — so the mean sits above the median. A projection of 2.7 against a line of 2.5 is a positive Diff and still an under, because more than half of all outcomes finish at two or fewer. Trust the probability, not the difference; the difference is shown because it is what everyone looks for first.
Flag definitions

Flags are the shortlist, not the model — they never move a projection. Each one marks a row where a specific, checkable condition is true, and hovering a chip on the board shows that row’s actual numbers. A green chip is a reason to look; an amber chip is a reason to be careful.

VALUE
ERA is at least 0.85 runs above SIERA — he has pitched better than his line score says, and the market tends to price the line score. Needs four starts before it can fire, because the gap is meaningless on two.
REGRESS
The same gap the other way: ERA at least 0.85 runs below SIERA. Sequencing and defence have been doing work the pitcher has not, and neither travels.
WHIFF
Both sides of a strikeout matchup line up: SwStr% at or above 12.8% into a lineup that strikes out in 23.5% or more of its plate appearances. The K projection already accounts for this; the flag says the two effects are stacking rather than cancelling.
LEASH
Fewer than five innings projected. Every counting prop is capped by the outing rather than by the stuff — the most common way a good strikeout matchup still misses its number.
PARK
A venue with a run factor of 112 or higher. The park term is capped inside the context score so one ballpark cannot dominate it, and this flag is what the cap hides.
Model constants live in SCORING, LEASH and ENV; the sample generator is buildSampleSlate(). All in app.js.
🚏 Mind the gap — these are projections, not promises. All aboard: built for the Chew Choo Station Discord. 🚂
